facts.fact_text: The applicants participated in an assembly on 6 May 2014.
According to the applicants, they were among people who gathered near the Baku Assize Court on 6 May 2014 to support members of Nida (an opposition group) who were being tried on that day.
The courtroom of the Baku Assize Court was full on 6 May 2014, and therefore some people gathered outside the court to wait for the outcome of the proceedings.
When the Baku Assize Court announced its judgment on 6 May 2014, those who had gathered outside began to protest against the judgment, considering it unfair.
Immediately after the protesters started chanting slogans on 6 May 2014, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the demonstration near the Baku Assize Court.
The applicants were arrested during the dispersal operation on 6 May 2014.
After their arrest, the applicants were taken to a police station.
The applicants were kept overnight at the police station.
The applicants were questioned at the police station.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the first applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Nasimi District Court convicted the second applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the first applicant to a period of administrative detention of thirty days.
The Nasimi District Court sentenced the second applicant to a period of administrative detention of twenty days.

The administrative-offence reports issued against the applicants stated that they had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan: participation in a public assembly organised not in accordance with the law.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced, for the first time, punishments in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days or community service for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan.
Immediately after the protesters started chanting slogans on 6 May 2014, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the demonstration near the Baku Assize Court.
The applicants were arrested during the dispersal operation on 6 May 2014.
After their arrest, the applicants were taken to a police station.
The applicants were kept overnight at the police station.
The applicants were questioned at the police station.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer while they were in police custody.
According to a police officer's decision and an order dated 6 May 2014, a State-funded lawyer, Mr A.B., was invited to defend the second applicant.
According to the applicants, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court (first-instance court) was very brief in the case of the first applicant.
According to the applicants, the hearing before the Nasimi District Court (first-instance court) was very brief in the case of the second applicant.

According to the applicants, members of the public were not allowed inside the courtroom during the hearings before the Nasimi District Court, even though the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
According to the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing before the Nasimi District Court.
According to the transcript of the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant, the State-funded lawyer Mr O.A. did not make any oral or written submissions.

The only witnesses questioned during the hearing before the Nasimi District Court concerning the first applicant were police officers who, according to official records, had arrested her or issued the administrative-offence report on her.
With respect to the second applicant, the Nasimi District Court did not question any witness.
